Adjacent couples: treat each couple as a block, giving (3−1)!·2^3=16 circular arrangements. Opposite couples: fix one person by rotation; choose which opposite pair is occupied by each of the other two couples (2 ways) and orient each pair (2^2), giving 8. Total 24.

The allowed same-country pairs are edges in the 2×3 seat grid: horizontal or vertical adjacency. The 2×3 ladder has 3 perfect matchings. Assign the three countries to these pairs in 3! ways and the two students within each country to endpoints in 2^3 ways: 3·6·8=144.
For each k, the inner sum excludes the two endpoint binomial coefficients, so it equals 2^(2k)−2. At k=1,2,3 these are 2,14,62; total 78.

In that excluded case, black in B,C must each be positive (4 distributions), while white in A,B,C with A positive has C(5,2)=10 distributions. Exclude 40, leaving 275.
